beginner.headline: New Hunger Games Actors Feel Excited and Nervous
beginner.brief: The new Hunger Games film is called Sunrise on the Reaping. Its story takes place 24 years before the first Hunger Games film. The three main actors are Joseph Zada, Mckenna Grace and Whitney Peak. They felt excited and nervous before the film came out. Zada plays a young Haymitch, a character from the earlier films. He watched the earlier films and made notes to prepare for his part. Grace worked as an actor when she was a child. Peak and Zada asked Grace for help when they felt confused while talking about the film. One actor says they are thankful to have each other. The film is now in cinemas.

intermediate.headline: New Hunger Games Stars Find Support in Each Other
intermediate.brief: Joseph Zada, Mckenna Grace and Whitney Peak have the leading roles in the Hunger Games prequel Sunrise on the Reaping. A prequel tells an earlier part of a story, and this film is set 24 years before the original Hunger Games. Before the release, the three actors showed excitement and worry as they began a demanding series of press interviews. Zada, who plays Haymitch Abernathy, said the actors stayed close and made sure everyone felt supported. Grace is the most experienced of the three, with a career beginning in childhood that includes television series and recent Ghostbusters films. However, she said that joining the Hunger Games series was unlike anything she had experienced before. Peak said she and Zada turned to Grace when confused during film promotion, and Zada described Grace as a mentor. Zada plays a teenage version of Haymitch, the role played by Woody Harrelson in the original films. To develop his performance, Zada spent months studying Harrelson's acting in the first four Hunger Games films and taking notes. He used this research as a starting point while adding his own ideas to the role. Peak said filming could quickly become overwhelming, so the actors tried to keep the mood light between difficult scenes. Grace explained that sharing physically and emotionally difficult work helped the cast form close relationships.

advanced.headline: New Hunger Games Cast Confront Pressure Through Mutual Support
advanced.brief: Sunrise on the Reaping places Joseph Zada, Mckenna Grace and Whitney Peak at the centre of the latest Hunger Games instalment. Set 24 years before the original film, it adapts Suzanne Collins’ 2025 novel of the same name. The sixth film joins a series whose worldwide earnings have exceeded $3.3 billion since 2012. Beginning a gruelling press run, the trio showed a mixture of anticipation, anxiety and excitement surrounding the release. Grace brings substantial screen experience, including appearances in The Handmaid’s Tale and two recent Ghostbusters films. Nevertheless, she described joining the franchise as deeply unsettling and unlike anything her previous work had prepared her for. Peak joked that she and Zada repeatedly sought out Grace when they felt stuck or confused while promoting the film, while Zada described her as a mentor. Zada plays the teenage Haymitch, a District 12 participant portrayed by Woody Harrelson in the original films. Reviews have been generally positive, with several outlets praising Zada while acknowledging the difficulty of stepping into Harrelson's shoes. Having spent months studying Harrelson’s earlier portrayals, Zada used his research as a foundation for his own interpretation. When they met halfway through filming, Harrelson recommended Cool Hand Luke, which Zada said helped ground his portrayal, and Harold and Maud, which he described as an enjoyable watch. Jesse Plemons regarded Zada’s role as a substantial undertaking and expressed admiration for his stamina and composure. An ensemble cast including Ralph Fiennes, Maya Hawke, Kieran Culkin and Elle Fanning returns audiences to a brutal dystopian world during the fiftieth Hunger Games. Within that fictional society, the ruling Capitol organises annual games involving Panem’s twelve districts as punishment for rebellion. Peak described the work as intensely stressful at times, making lighter moments between difficult scenes particularly valuable. Grace linked the cast’s close bonds to the days they spent sharing physically strenuous and emotionally intense work.
